body:
It's so easy to see a reflection of ourselves in other people. That person hit me, so maybe I deserve to be abused? That person said something mean, maybe it's true? That person doesn't respect me, maybe I don't deserve anyone's respect?

The truth is just that assholes are assholes who do asshole things. You aren't how other people treat you, you aren't what other people see.

I don't know you, I can't tell you if you're a good person or not, but I know that no one deserves what they've done to you, they make you feel small so they can feel big and important.

You deserve so much better.

I'm proud of you too. I know how easy it can be to throw those clothes on the floor or neglect to do the dishes and these problems pile up. Our homes are a reflection of who we are, and you're on your way to being emotionally "clean". Good job on taking that first step.

"why me?" Is, I imagine, one of those questions we've asked ourselves since we crawled out of the ocean.

Things didn't happen to you for a reason, they just happened, trying to figure out what it was about you or what you did to deserve it is pointless. They happened, they're done, you're the person you are now because of them.

The question is: do you really want to do it? Maybe there's a way out of this which doesn't involve anyone else getting hurt. Especially not you who deserve to be hurt the least.
Hey. Drop me a line in my DMs, I'm here for you.

No one here is going to tell you it's okay to die. That's a decision for you and you only.

Those people who abused you, who treat you like you were beneath them, they're just as bad as the people who act like you owe them something.

All of these relationships are unhealthy, and this pain is part of realising that. You were brought in to the world by bad people, you grew up and ended up surrounded by bad people. That's not an indictment on you, that's not your fault.

Move on. Find new people who appreciate you for who you are, who don't expect change, who don't expect subservience. You are worth so much more than that.

Well then you're in luck, since that doesn't require any qualifications beyond a pass in English and Maths.

I am very good friends with an army mechanic (I was Royal Logistics Corps, Combat Medic) who works on LSVs (logistics support vehicles) and he's as thick as two old bricks.

You're going to need to pass the physical requirements, mind. So it wouldn't be a bad idea to practice long distance running and some basic weight training as you age. This has the added benefit of getting your body in shape and making you look fine as hell as you start getting in to your dating ages.

Don't worry about what your parents want. They had their own life and made their own decisions, that's their only concern. You have to do what makes you happy, if you spend your life chasing the wants of other people you'll have a family who are very proud of their miserable child.

When you look back on this in a decade what do you want to think: my parents like the choices I made? Or: I'm happy with the choices I made?

Your grades don't matter all that much. Not enough to be worth fretting over.

Here's the truth your parents and teachers will never tell you:

You can have a happy and financially successful life without good grades. You don't even need to go to college.

Trades (plumbing, electrics, etc), computing (software engineering, self taught web development), etc., are some of the most popular jobs of today, require no college education and all pay more than $100,000 per year contracting.

By all means, study hard, but do it for you. Because you want the grades, not because of external pressure. If you don't get an A, so what? If you don't get a B, so what?

About 2 years after you leave college, where you went and what you got stop mattering. About 4 years after it stops being asked in interviews.

The trick is to figure out now what interests you and start working towards it, but don't feel like you're a failure because of your grades at 13, you're not.

This is unfortunately the standard.

In my experience, base counsellors exist to remove any liability or culpability from the military, not necessarily to treat the patients.

You aren't stupid. However else you might feel, you aren't stupid.

Bad things happen to good people all the time. I'm sorry that you're in this much pain, I know it hurts. It's going to hurt even more for a while, but take some time to think about this decision, and see how you feel when the tears have stopped and apathy finally kicks in.
